info.name: PayFlow
info.description:
Local development collection for the PayFlow stack.

- baseUrl = http://localhost:5050 (Gateway). YARP routes /api/* to the matching service.
- Demo flow: Register Tenant → Login → POST /api/transactions (merchant-facing). Internally Transaction calls Payment over HTTP; the merchant sees only the final result.
- Login's test script captures `accessToken` into {{token}}; protected requests send `Authorization: Bearer {{token}}` automatically.
- The Payments group hits /api/payments/charge directly — that endpoint is internal in real architecture (Transaction calls it) but stays Postman-testable for adapter-level demos.
- Postgres on host port 5433 (psql -h localhost -p 5433 -U payflow -d payflow).

Start the services with:
    dotnet run --project src/Services/Identity/PayFlow.Identity.API        # :5001
    dotnet run --project src/Services/Payment/PayFlow.Payment.API          # :5002
    dotnet run --project src/Services/Transaction/PayFlow.Transaction.API  # :5003
    dotnet run --project src/ApiGateway/PayFlow.Gateway                    # :5050

request.description: Liveness probe. Returns 200 OK with body 'Healthy' when the service is up and the DB is reachable.

Reconciliation has no public business endpoints yet (those land with the refund saga in M4.D). The gateway has no /api/reconciliation route, so probe the service directly on its dev port to confirm it boots, applies migrations, and the outbox/Kafka wiring is alive.
Notification liveness.
Webhooks API health probe; no auth required.

Registers a tenant + initial admin atomically.
Expected: 201 Created, Location header, body { tenantId, adminUserId, slug }.

Re-sending the same slug after the happy path ran.
Expected: 409 Conflict, ValidationProblemDetails with errors.Slug = ["TENANT_SLUG_TAKEN"]. Same body shape as 422s — only status differs.

Email shape check inside the Domain VO.
Expected: 422 ValidationProblemDetails, errors.AdminEmail = ["EMAIL_INVALID"].

Caught by FluentValidation before the command reaches the handler.
Expected: 422 ValidationProblemDetails, errors.AdminPassword = ["TOO_SHORT"].

Slug is normalised to lowercase + dashes only; spaces are rejected by the regex inside Tenant.Create.
Expected: 422 ValidationProblemDetails, errors.Slug = ["TENANT_SLUG_INVALID"].

FluentValidation catches the blank Name before the handler runs.
Expected: 422 ValidationProblemDetails, errors.Name = ["REQUIRED"].

Stripe mock: always Captured (sale flow).
Expected: 200 OK with status = "Captured", providerReference starting with 'ch_'.

Iyzico mock: returns Authorized only (its real flow is auth-then-capture).
Expected: 200 OK with status = "Authorized", providerReference starting with 'iyz_'.

PayPal mock with amount NOT ending in 13 or 99.
Expected: 200 OK with status = "Captured".

PayPal mock test gate: amount ending in 13.
Expected: 200 OK with status = "SoftDeclined", declineCode = "INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS", providerReference = null. (Routing would fail over to the next provider in the rule.)

PayPal mock test gate: amount ending in 99.
Expected: 200 OK with status = "HardDeclined", declineCode = "DO_NOT_HONOR". (Routing would stop and not try other providers.)
Expected: 422 ValidationProblemDetails, errors.ProviderCode = ["PROVIDER_NOT_CONFIGURED"].
Expected: 422 ValidationProblemDetails, errors.AmountMinor = ["MUST_BE_POSITIVE"].

Expects the tenant + admin created by 'Register Tenant — Happy Path' to exist.
Expected: 200 OK with body { accessToken, expiresAt, userId, tenantId }.
The test script stores accessToken/userId/tenantId in collection variables so subsequent requests can use them.

Expected: 401 Unauthorized, code = AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS.
Identical response to 'unknown email' and 'unknown tenant slug' — the endpoint deliberately collapses all credential mismatches into one code so it can't be used as an enumeration oracle.
Expected: same 401 + AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS as wrong password.

FluentValidation rejects blank fields before the handler runs.
Expected: 422 with errors map { TenantSlug: [REQUIRED], Email: [REQUIRED], Password: [REQUIRED] }.

Run 'Login — Happy Path' first so {{token}} is populated.
Expected: 200 OK with body { userId, tenantId, email, displayName, roles[] } reflecting the JWT's claims.

JwtBearer middleware rejects requests without a valid Authorization header.
Expected: 401 Unauthorized.

Malformed or unsigned token fails validation.
Expected: 401 Unauthorized.

Routing config is [paypal, stripe]. Amount 14990 has no special digits, so paypal captures on the first try.
Expected: 201 Created, status="Captured", providerCode="paypal", attempts.length == 1.

item.name: Create Transaction — Failover (paypal Soft → stripe Capture)
Create Transaction — Hard Decline Stops Failover

request.description:
Amount ending in 99 makes the paypal mock HardDecline. Stripe is NEVER asked — hard declines say "the card is bad, trying elsewhere won't help."
Expected: 201 (the API call itself succeeded), status="Failed", failureReason="HardDeclined", providerCode="paypal", attempts.length == 1.

Click TWICE in a row.
- 1st click: 201 Created. The handler ran, the transaction row was inserted, the response was stored in Redis at idem:{tenant}:/api/transactions:fixed-replay-key-001 with 24h TTL.
- 2nd click: 201 Created with the SAME transactionId AND a response header `Idempotency-Replayed: true`. The handler did NOT run; the Redis-cached response was returned verbatim. Exactly the retry-safety contract from docs/api/idempotency.md.

item.name: Create Transaction — Same Key, Different Body (422)

request.description:
Run 'Idempotent Replay' first so the fixed key is in Redis.
Then run this — same key, different body (different amount + currency + order ref).
Expected: 422 ProblemDetails with code IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED_DIFFERENT_BODY. This signals a client-side bug: the same operation-id was used for two different logical operations.

Idempotency-Key is required on POST /api/transactions.
Expected: 400 ProblemDetails with code IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED.

RequireAuthorization() on the endpoint group rejects this before the handler runs.
Expected: 401 Unauthorized.

Run twice with different Idempotency-Key but the SAME order_reference (the fixed body).
- 1st click: 201 Created (idempotency key is fresh, order_reference is also fresh).
- 2nd click: a fresh Idempotency-Key but the same order_reference — now the application-level uniqueness check kicks in.
Expected on 2nd: 409 ValidationProblemDetails, errors.OrderReference = ["ORDER_REFERENCE_ALREADY_USED"]. (Idempotency is per-key, order_reference uniqueness is per-tenant.)

FluentValidation catches non-3-letter currency.
Expected: 422 ValidationProblemDetails, errors.Currency = ["LENGTH_3"].
Expected: 422 ValidationProblemDetails, errors.AmountMinor = ["MUST_BE_POSITIVE"].

item.name: Refunds
item.description:
Refund saga starts here. The Transaction service writes a refund row + the `payflow.refund.requested.v1` outbox event in one SaveChanges; the Reconciliation service (M4 follow-up) consumes that event and walks the rest of the saga.

Run `Create Transaction — Happy Path` first — its test script captures `{{transactionId}}` into the collection.

request.description:
Partial refund (5000 of a 14990 capture). Expected: 202 Accepted, `Location` header to the refund resource, response `status="Requested"`. The outbox interceptor writes `payflow.refund.requested.v1` in the same SaveChanges; Reconciliation picks it up downstream.

Note: the body carries only `amountMinor`. RequestedBy is always sourced from the JWT `sub` claim server-side — the request type has no audit field so a caller cannot smuggle a free-form string (e.g. an email) into the outbox / Kafka payload.
Requesting a refund larger than the captured amount (counting any in-flight Requested/Processing refunds). Expected: 422 with `errors.AmountMinor = ["REFUND_AMOUNT_EXCEEDS_REMAINING"]`.
Refund against a non-existent transaction id. Expected: 404 with `code = TRANSACTION_NOT_FOUND`.
Idempotency middleware applies to all POSTs under /api/transactions, including refunds. Expected: 400 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED`.

Polls the refund. Run "Request Refund — Happy Path" first to populate {{refundId}}; wait a second or two for the saga to walk (Requested → Processing → Completed), then this returns the terminal state.

Direct hit on the Payment service refund endpoint — bypasses the saga. Useful for: poking the provider mocks directly, verifying the test-card behaviour (paypal: amount % 100 == 13 → Declined), debugging without Kafka in the loop. Not what merchants use; the real flow is the refund saga.

item.name: Reports
item.description:
CQRS read-side. Reporting consumes payflow.transaction.* and payflow.refund.completed.v1 from Kafka and projects them into per-tenant, per-day, per-currency buckets. The query endpoint reads those buckets — tenant scoping comes from the JWT.

Run a few Create Transactions + a Refund Happy Path first to seed the projection, then hit this endpoint.

item.name: GET Transactions Summary (last 30 days, all currencies)

request.description: Default window: last 30 days UTC, every currency. Reporting runs on port 5005 (no gateway route yet). Expected: 200 with one row per (date, currency) bucket — attempted / captured / failed counts plus refund counters.
Same view filtered to a single currency bucket. Pass any 3-letter ISO code; unknown ones return an empty rows array (not an error).
from / to must be ISO yyyy-MM-dd. Anything else → 422 with `errors.from = ["INVALID_DATE"]`.
Reporting liveness — also the easiest way to confirm migrations applied + the consumer background service is up.
Registers a subscription for the calling tenant. Response includes the HMAC secret EXACTLY ONCE — store it immediately. Subsequent list/get endpoints omit the secret.
Subscription URL must be http or https. Anything else returns 422 ValidationProblem with `Subscription = [URL_SCHEME_UNSUPPORTED]` (propagated from the domain `WebhookSubscription.Create` Result).
FluentValidation rejects empty event type before the domain constructor runs. Expected: 422 with `eventType` error key.
Tenant-scoped list. Returns id, eventType, url, isActive, createdAt per subscription. **Secret is intentionally omitted** — merchants who lose the secret rotate by creating a new subscription.
Soft-delete: the row stays in the DB with `is_active=false` and a `deactivated_at` timestamp for the audit trail; future fan-outs skip it. Run the happy-path above first to capture the id.
Tenant scope + id mismatch returns 404 with no body.

Latest N delivery rows for the tenant. State is one of `Pending` / `Sent` / `Failed`. Use this to debug an integration: a failing endpoint shows up as repeated `Pending` rows with `nextAttemptAt` advancing (exponential backoff, 5 attempts), and a 4xx receiver shows up as `Failed` rows with a status code.

item.name: Notifications
item.description: Read-side notification log. The service is consume-only: it tails `payflow.transaction.captured.v1`, `payflow.refund.completed.v1`, and `payflow.refund.failed.v1` from Kafka, renders an email template for each, and writes the audit row in `notification.notifications`. The endpoint below replays whatever the dev `LoggingEmailSender` would have sent.

request.description: Run Create Transaction first to seed a TransactionCaptured notification, then this returns the rendered subject/body/status for the tenant in the JWT.
Same view with an explicit cap. Server clamps `take` to [1, 200].
